payload.sensitivity: The J1-first sequencing is nearly flip-proof by construction: because J2 layers on J1's output with zero rework, no weight perturbation makes building J1 first WRONG - the worst any weighting does is demand J2's layer sooner. The only genuine flip world: the owner's first board round finds native collapse/expand unusable for the long gate briefs (deep nesting, no search) - then J2 stops being optional and becomes the T1 pass-line carrier. Credible - the owner demonstrably reads these panes hard (the maximize and scroll complaints).
payload.tripwires: One RAID watch-item: T-J2 - at the first board round over a real gate detail, the owner judges the native tree; if reading a deep brief still hurts, the J2 layer builds in the same iteration (pre-approved at convergence, no new gate needed). Owner: the owner, at the board round. No other credible flips.
